units.required_action: Wide eye-level listening triangle: Medhas faces Suratha and Samādhi across a low fire; their neutral attention is labeled visual adaptation and adds no reaction or motive.
Medium speaker-anchored view of Medhas beginning the distinction, with both listeners present in quiet profile and the upper field reserved for lettering.
Close view of Medhas's open hand above the low fire; smoke and navy negative space begin the transition without becoming a supernatural source claim.
Wide frame of the three listeners reduced to silhouettes as the dark upper field opens toward the dissolution sequence; no invented listener reaction.
Full-page horizonless dissolution water: no shore, mountain, city, temple, star map or ordinary landmark; scale comes only from sparse gold reflections and layered darkness.

Low horizontal full-page repose: sleeping Viṣṇu is clearly supported by Śeṣa above the flood; Yoganidrā is a non-anatomical sleep field, with no fixed halo, weapon, body residence or conventional arm/hood count.
Vertical establishing panel: the lotus rises from Viṣṇu to lotus-seated Brahmā while Śeṣa remains visibly below; do not add a temple, throne room or invented island.
Medium lotus-level view of Brahmā with only flood beyond; exact head and arm counts remain source-silent and no conventional multiplicity is asserted.
Narrow closing panel of still water and a dark approaching interval, carrying danger without yet revealing invented detail.

Full-page opposing depth: Madhu and Kaiṭabha emerge into the water near Viṣṇu's ear-region and advance toward Brahmā's lotus; show no anatomical gore, genealogy, weapons, army or motive beyond the threat.
Brahmā's sightline connects the approaching pair to sleeping Viṣṇu below; keep lotus, sleepers and threat in one stable vertical geography.
Tight panel on the narrowing water gap between the demons and lotus, with no invented weapon or attack contact.
Wide three-level hold: demons on water, Viṣṇu on Śeṣa, Brahmā above; Yoganidrā remains a sleep field, not a body-locus figure.
Medium lotus-level view: Brahmā turns his attention toward Yoganidrā rather than shouting at Viṣṇu; the demons remain distant but advancing.
Quiet close view of Brahmā in gathered attention with a protected dialogue field; do not add weapons, multi-head iconography or an unsourced halo.

Full-page devotional address from Brahmā toward the source-neutral field of Yoganidrā; keep the hymn attributed to its speaker and do not literalize its cosmic names as independent project facts or add a weapon array.
Brahmā's appeal is directed toward Yoganidrā while the advancing pair remains in the same spatial lane; no escape route is invented.
Closing stillness around Viṣṇu: six subtle source-named locus groups prepare for withdrawal without implying that Yoganidrā permanently resides inside any body part.

Full-page exact-locus withdrawal map: distinct radiance leaves Viṣṇu's eyes, mouth, nose, arms, heart and breast, then gathers as a separate appeared presence before Brahmā; keep all six groups readable, modest and non-anatomical, with no seventh locus or permanent-residence implication.
Close view of Viṣṇu's eyes opening after the withdrawal; the same sleeping identity shifts to alertness without an invented transformation.
Wide re-establishing view: awake Viṣṇu sees Brahmā and both Asuras while Śeṣa remains the stable support and Yoganidrā stands apart before Brahmā.
Viṣṇu rises into the water action lane while Madhu and Kaiṭabha turn from the lotus; maintain left-to-right approach continuity.
Arm-to-arm engagement begins with three coherent humanlike silhouettes; no army, weapon, wound or unsupported arm count.
Wide hold on the three combatants against the unbounded flood; Yoganidrā and Brahmā remain distant witnesses, not combatants.
Madhu drives forward and Viṣṇu checks him with an anatomically coherent grappling hold; Kaiṭabha remains a separate flank threat.
Kaiṭabha closes from the side as Viṣṇu turns; preserve all three silhouettes and show no weapon or injury.
The trio separates into a readable triangle that can cycle again, with wave direction carrying the eye back to panel one.

Full-page nonliteral time image: one central arm-to-arm tableau is surrounded by repeated wave-rings and changing light bands rather than duplicate bodies, clocks or a literal count of years; no weapons, army or injury.
A repeated struggle rhythm shows one Asura pressing whenever the other falls back; use only arm-to-arm action and no invented strategy.

The struggle pauses as Madhu and Kaiṭabha's posture shifts to pride under Yoganidrā's deluding power; render the influence as source-neutral spatial distortion, not mind-control anatomy or a new motive.
The three combatants stand apart after the long struggle; Madhu and Kaiṭabha occupy equal boon-giver positions without a victory throne or invented ritual.
Quiet reaction hold on Viṣṇu receiving the joint offer; no thought text, weapon or added motive.
Medium triangular dialogue frame: Viṣṇu answers both joint boon-givers directly, with no discus yet raised and no defeat locus implied.
Wide still-water hold after the words, keeping all three figures separate and the flood unbroken.
Wide panel of flood in every direction as Madhu states the first half of the joint condition; no dry place is yet shown.
Balanced two-shot of Madhu and Kaiṭabha completing the condition jointly, with neither replaced by an outside boon-giver.
Close dialogue hold on Viṣṇu's acceptance; do not preview any thigh, lap, buttocks or other anatomical solution.
The flood still surrounds all three figures while a distinct dry-earth plane enters the composition away from every body; its mechanism, geography and size remain unspecified.
Overhead geometry confirms water around a separate unflooded earth area without placing either demon on Viṣṇu's thigh, lap, buttocks or any other bodily locus.

Full-page decisive composition: all three stand on or beside the clearly separate unflooded earth plane, Viṣṇu raises the sourced discus, and the swift luminous circle ends the threat through silhouettes and motion only; show no wound, anatomical impact point, thigh/lap/buttocks platform or graphic body detail.
Quiet return to the same hermitage geometry: Medhas lets the account rest while Suratha and Samādhi remain neutral listeners with no invented spoken reaction.
Close on the low fire settling beneath a protected final caption field; no next-book hook or new doctrinal symbol.
Text-led ivory source-note page with a restrained navy-and-gold forest-frame border; no character figure, mythic reenactment, source quotation styling or new iconographic claim.
Text-led family-reflection page with a quiet fire-and-tree ornamental border only; no character speech balloon, sacred quotation styling or implied scriptural status.
